'''Changpeng Zhao''' ({{lang-zh|t=赵长鹏|p=Zhào Chángpéng}}; born 1977), commonly known as '''CZ''', is a Canadian businessman who is known for co-founding the cryptocurrency company [[Binance]]. He has also served as CTO of [[OKX|OKCoin]] and CEO of Binance. According to ''[[Forbes]],'' Zhao is the richest Canadian and the [[The World's Billionaires|17th-richest person in the world]], with a [[net worth]] estimated at $111.1{{Nbsp}}billion {{as of|2026|04|lc=y|post=.}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=Changpeng Zhao |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/changpeng-zhao/ |access-date=2026-04-26 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>

He resigned as the CEO of Binance in November 2023 after the [[United States Department of Justice|U.S Department of Justice]] alleged he violated the [[Bank Secrecy Act]] and the [[International Emergency Economic Powers Act]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Sigalos|first1=MacKenzie|last2=Browne|first2=Ryan|date=November 22, 2023|title=Binance users pull more than $1 billion from the exchange after CEO leaves, pleads guilty|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2023/11/22/whats-next-for-binance-after-doj-settlement-departure-of-changpeng-zhao.html|access-date=December 5, 2023|website=[[CNBC]]|language=en|archive-date=December 5, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231205025607/https://www.cnbc.com/2023/11/22/whats-next-for-binance-after-doj-settlement-departure-of-changpeng-zhao.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="wsjNov23" /> He pleaded guilty and was sentenced to four months in prison in April 2024.<ref name="wsjNov23" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Browne |first=MacKenzie Sigalos, Ryan |date=April 30, 2024 |title=Binance founder Changpeng Zhao sentenced to 4 months in prison after plea deal |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2024/04/30/binance-founder-changpeng-zhao-cz-sentenced-to-four-months-in-prison-.html |access-date=April 30, 2024 |website=CNBC |language=en |archive-date=April 30, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430191443/https://www.cnbc.com/2024/04/30/binance-founder-changpeng-zhao-cz-sentenced-to-four-months-in-prison-.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Zhao completed his sentence by September of the same year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zeff |first=Maxwell |date=September 27, 2024 |title=Binance founder 'CZ' released from custody after four-month sentence |url=https://techcrunch.com/2024/09/27/binance-founder-cz-released-from-custody-after-four-month-sentence/ |website=techcrunch.com}}</ref> In October 2025, Zhao was given a [[Presidential pardon in the United States|presidential pardon]] by President [[Donald Trump]].<ref name="wsjoct2025" />

== Early life and education==
Changpeng Zhao was born in [[Ganyu]] in China's [[Jiangsu|Jiangsu province]].<ref name="RStone">{{Cite magazine |last=Gottsegen |first=Will |date=June 3, 2023 |title=Crypto's Richest Man Is Waiting Out the Chaos |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/culture-features/changpeng-zhao-cz-crypto-binance-1234740435/ |magazine=Rolling Stone |language=en-US |access-date=October 5, 2023 |archive-date=December 2, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231202132243/https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/culture-features/changpeng-zhao-cz-crypto-binance-1234740435/ |url-status=live }}</ref> His parents were both schoolteachers in China.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 21, 2023 |title=Who is Changpeng Zhao (CZ), the Founder of Binance? |url=https://en.coinotag.com/who-is-changpeng-zhao-cz-the-founder-of-binance-1/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231013231010/https://en.coinotag.com/who-is-changpeng-zhao-cz-the-founder-of-binance-1/ |archive-date=October 13, 2023 |access-date=September 21, 2023 |website=en.coinotag.com}}</ref> His father Zhao Shengkai<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 28, 2023 |title=Crossing the Digital Storm: The Legend of Zhao Changpeng and Binance - CaptainZ |url=https://captainz.xlog.app/chuan-yue-shu-zi-feng-bao--zhao-chang-peng-yu-bi-an-de-chuan-qi-md |access-date=2025-10-12 |website=Crossing the Digital Storm: The Legend of Zhao Changpeng and Binance - CaptainZ |language=en}}</ref> worked as a university instructor before he was branded a "pro-[[Bourgeoisie|bourgeois]] intellect" and [[exile]]d to rural areas shortly after Zhao's birth.<ref>{{Cite web |title=赵长鹏与币安的崛起 |url=https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/338426558 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230618171240/http://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/338426558 |archive-date=June 18, 2023 |access-date=November 9, 2021 |website=知乎专栏 |language=zh}}</ref> In late 1989, when he was 12 years old, he acquired a Canadian visa in 1989 and emigrated with his family to Canada after the [[1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre|Tiananmen Square protests and massacre]].<ref name=":0" /> They settled down in [[Vancouver|Vancouver, British Columbia]]. During his teenage years in Canada, Zhao helped to support his family by holding down a number of [[Tertiary sector of the economy|service]] jobs, including working as a fast-food clerk at a [[McDonald's]] restaurant and a gas station.<ref name="Ambler 2018">{{Cite news |last=Ambler |first=Pamela |date=February 28, 2018 |title=From Zero To Crypto Billionaire In Under A Year: Meet The Founder Of Binance |work=Forbes |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/pamelaambler/2018/02/07/changpeng-zhao-binance-exchange-crypto-cryptocurrency/ |access-date=March 8, 2018 |archive-date=September 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925222533/https://www.forbes.com/sites/pamelaambler/2018/02/07/changpeng-zhao-binance-exchange-crypto-cryptocurrency// |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="NPR20230813flipper">{{Cite news |last=Gura |first=David |date=August 13, 2023 |title=The future of crypto hinges on a fight between the SEC and a former burger flipper |work=NPR |url=https://www.npr.org/2023/08/13/1188231308/binance-lawsuits-cz-crypto-sec-coinbase-bitcoin |access-date=August 13, 2023 |archive-date=August 13, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230813100604/https://www.npr.org/2023/08/13/1188231308/binance-lawsuits-cz-crypto-sec-coinbase-bitcoin |url-status=live }}</ref>

Zhao attended [[McGill University School of Computer Science|McGill University]] in [[Montreal|Montreal, Quebec]], where he majored in [[computer science]].<ref name="Ambler 2018" />

== Career ==
After graduating from McGill, Zhao was selected for an internship in [[Tokyo]] working for a subcontractor of the [[Tokyo Stock Exchange]], developing software for [[Order matching system|matching trade orders]]. He later went to work full-time for four years at [[Bloomberg Tradebook]], where he was a developer of [[Futures contract|futures trading]] software.<ref name="Ambler 2018" />

In 2005, Zhao moved to [[Shanghai]] to launch his business career, where he established his first technology startup company called Fusion Systems,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Russell |first=Jon |date=May 4, 2018 |title=Catch Binance CEO Changpeng&nbsp;Zhao at TechCrunch's blockchain event on July 6 |url=https://techcrunch.com/2018/05/04/binance-ceo-changpeng-zhao-techcrunch-blockchain-event/ |access-date=May 4, 2018 |website=TechCrunch |archive-date=February 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226134529/https://techcrunch.com/2018/05/04/binance-ceo-changpeng-zhao-techcrunch-blockchain-event/ |url-status=live }}</ref> which was known for "some of the fastest automated [[high-frequency trading]] platforms and systems for [[stockbroker]]s."<ref name="Ambler 2018" /> Zhao first heard of bitcoin in 2013 when playing poker with Bobby Lee (brother of [[Charlie Lee (computer scientist)|Charlie Lee]]) who would later go on to found [[BTCC (company)|BTCC]]. Lee advised Zhao to put 10% of his money into bitcoin. Zhao instead "went all in" and sold his apartment in Shanghai and invested all of his wealth in bitcoin, much to his family's dismay.<ref name="NPR20230813flipper" /> Zhao then began joining cryptocurrency-based projects, becoming the third member of the team that developed [[Blockchain.info]], working as the company's head of development for eight months, and he also served as [[chief technology officer]] of OKCoin for less than a year.<ref name="Ambler 2018" />

In 2022, Zhao invested $500 million through Binance to finance the [[acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Crypto CEO says Elon Musk has no plan for Twitter, and reveals why he wrote him a $500 million 'blank check' |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/elon-musk-twitter-deal-binance-ceo-investment-business-plan-crypto-2022-5 |website=[[Business Insider]] |access-date=May 6, 2022 |archive-date=May 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220506161127/https://www.businessinsider.com/elon-musk-twitter-deal-binance-ceo-investment-business-plan-crypto-2022-5 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On April 7, 2024, he was appointed by the [[Ministry of Finance (Pakistan)|Pakistan Ministry of Finance]] as a strategic advisor to the [[Pakistan Crypto Council]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 9, 2025 |title=Binance founder becomes advisor to president on digital asset development |url=https://www.akchabar.kg/en/news/osnovatel-kompanii-binance-chanpen-chzhao-stal-sovetnikom-prezidenta-po-voprosam-kasayushchimsya-razvitiya-tsifrovikh-aktivov-isssejvzqqnvzfgt |access-date=May 7, 2025 |website=Akchabar |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 3, 2025 |title=Основатель Binance Чанпэн Чжао стал советником Садыра Жапарова |url=https://kaktus.media/doc/523132_osnovatel_binance_chanpen_chjao_stal_sovetnikom_sadyra_japarova.html |access-date=May 7, 2025 |website=kaktus.media |language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Основатель криптобиржи Binance стал советником президента Кыргызстана по цифровым активам |url=https://fergana.agency/news/137756/ |access-date=May 7, 2025 |website=fergana.agency |language=ru}}</ref>

On May 3, 2025, he was appointed as an advisor to the president of [[Kyrgyzstan]], [[Sadyr Japarov]], on the development of digital assets.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 3, 2025 |title=Binance founder becomes advisor to president on digital asset development |url=https://www.akchabar.kg/en/news/osnovatel-kompanii-binance-chanpen-chzhao-stal-sovetnikom-prezidenta-po-voprosam-kasayushchimsya-razvitiya-tsifrovikh-aktivov-isssejvzqqnvzfgt |access-date=May 29, 2025 |website=akchabar.kg}}</ref>

===Binance===
After its launch in July 2017, the [[Binance]] [[cryptocurrency exchange]] was able to raise $15 million in an [[initial coin offering]], and trading began on the exchange eleven days later.<ref name="Lee 2018">{{Cite news |last1=Lee |first1=Justina |last2=Nakamura |first2=Yuji |last3=Robertson |first3=Benjamin |date=March 28, 2018 |title=How a Billionaire Crypto King Built the No. 1 Exchange in Just 8 Months |work=Bloomberg |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-03-28/crypto-s-billionaire-trading-king-has-suddenly-run-into-problems |access-date=May 4, 2018 }}</ref> In less than eight months, Zhao grew Binance into the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by [[Volume (finance)|trading volume]] (as of April 2018).<ref name="Cao 2018">{{Cite news |last=Cao |first=Sissi |date=April 3, 2018 |title=Despite Bitcoin Bubble Popping, Crypto Exchanges Are Making Billionaires Richer |work=Observer |url=http://observer.com/2018/04/ranking-most-profitable-cryptocurrency-exchanges/ |access-date=April 24, 2018 |archive-date=September 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925222506/https://observer.com/2018/04/ranking-most-profitable-cryptocurrency-exchanges// |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Lee 2018" /> Zhao also launched Binance Coin in 2017, a utility token that gives its owners various benefits, such as discounts on trading fees.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fee Structure on Binance |url=https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/115000429332 |access-date=September 12, 2022 |website=Binance.com |archive-date=September 12, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220912052459/https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/115000429332 |url-status=live }}</ref> In April 2019, Binance launched Binance Smart Chain, which has [[smart contract]] functionality and is an [[Ethereum]] competitor.

In February 2018, ''[[Forbes Magazine|Forbes]]'' placed him third on their list of "The Richest People In Cryptocurrency," with an estimated net worth of $1.1-2 billion.<ref name="Cao 2018" /><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Ambler |first1=Pamela |last2=Au-Yeung |first2=Angel |last3=Chung |first3=Grace |last4=Kauflin |first4=Jeff |last5=Konrad |first5=Alex |last6=Shin |first6=Laura |last7=Vardi |first7=Nathan |date=February 6, 2018 |title=The Richest People In Cryptocurrency |url=https://www.forbes.com/richest-in-cryptocurrency/ |access-date=March 8, 2018 |website=Forbes |archive-date=February 26, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180226033020/https://www.forbes.com/richest-in-cryptocurrency/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2019, Zhao launched Binance's U.S. affiliate, Binance.US.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our US Partner, Binance.US, Opens for Registration and Deposits {{!}} Binance |url=https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/360033855351 |access-date=July 11, 2022 |website=www.binance.com |archive-date=July 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220711061313/https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/360033855351 |url-status=live }}</ref> Binance withdrew its application to run a Singapore-based crypto exchange in 2021.<ref name="singapore">{{Cite web |title=Profile – Changpeng Zhao |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/changpeng-zhao/?sh=79b65c116277/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221126095939/https://fortune.com/2021/12/12/binance-singapore-drops-application-crypto-exchange-closes-richard-teng/ |archive-date=November 26, 2022 |access-date=April 12, 2023 |website=[[Forbes]]}}</ref>

==Legal troubles==
=== Civil lawsuits ===
On March 27, 2023, the [[Commodity Futures Trading Commission]] (CFTC) filed a lawsuit against Binance and Zhao in the [[United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois]], claiming willful evasion of US law and allegedly breaching derivatives rules.<ref name="bbcftc">{{cite news |title=Binance and Its CEO Sued by CFTC Over US Regulatory Violations |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-03-27/crypto-exchange-binance-sued-by-us-cftc-for-alleged-derivatives-rule-lapses |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=March 27, 2023 |access-date=March 27, 2023 |archive-date=November 17, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231117224516/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-03-27/crypto-exchange-binance-sued-by-us-cftc-for-alleged-derivatives-rule-lapses |url-status=live }}{{Subscription required}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=US regulator sues crypto exchange Binance and boss Changpeng Zhao |url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2023/mar/27/us-regulator-sues-crypto-exchange-binance-and-boss-changpeng-zhao |website=[[The Guardian]] |date=March 27, 2023 |access-date=March 27, 2023 |last1=Milmo |first1=Dan |archive-date=November 23, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123031933/https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2023/mar/27/us-regulator-sues-crypto-exchange-binance-and-boss-changpeng-zhao |url-status=live }}</ref> The agency accused Binance of breaking rules intended to thwart money laundering operations,<ref>{{cite news |title=Binance accused of breaking US financial laws |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-65091480 |website=[[BBC News]] |date=March 27, 2023 |access-date=March 28, 2023 |archive-date=November 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231101024927/https://www.bbc.com/news/business-65091480 |url-status=live }}</ref> pointing to internal communications describing transactions by Palestinian militant organization [[Hamas]] and suspected criminals.<ref name="bbcftc"/>

In June 2023, the [[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]] (SEC) sued Zhao and Binance on 13 charges for alleged violations of US securities rules.<ref>{{cite news |title=SEC Sues Binance and CEO Zhao for Breaking US Securities Rules |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-06-05/sec-sues-binance-and-ceo-zhao-for-breaking-us-securities-rules |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=June 5, 2023 |access-date=June 5, 2023 |archive-date=March 3, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260303175719/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-06-05/sec-sues-binance-and-ceo-zhao-for-breaking-us-securities-rules  }}{{Subscription required}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=S.E.C. Accuses Binance of Mishandling Funds and Lying to Regulators |work=The New York Times |date=June 5, 2023 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/06/05/business/sec-binance-charges.html |access-date=June 5, 2023 |archive-date=June 19, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230619232803/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/06/05/business/sec-binance-charges.html |last1=Goldstein |first1=Matthew |last2=Flitter |first2=Emily |last3=Yaffe-Bellany |first3=David }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Michaels |first1=Dave |last2=Ostroff |first2=Caitlin |last3=Kowsmann |first3=Patricia |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/money/companies/sec-sues-crypto-exchange-binance/ar-AA1c9vGS |title=SEC Sues Crypto Exchange Binance |work=[[Wall Street Journal]] |via=[[MSN News]] |date=June 5, 2023 |access-date=June 5, 2023 |archive-date=June 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230605212243/https://www.msn.com/en-us/money/companies/sec-sues-crypto-exchange-binance/ar-AA1c9vGS }}</ref>

In November 2024, [[FTX]] filed a lawsuit against [[Binance|Binance Holdings]] Ltd., Zhao, and other Binance executives, seeking to recover nearly $1.8 billion that FTX alleges was fraudulently transferred. The case centers on a July 2021 stock repurchase transaction in which Binance sold its stakes—approximately 20% of FTX's international unit and 18.4% of its U.S.-based entity—to FTX co-founder [[Sam Bankman-Fried]].<ref>{{Cite web|first= Emily| last=Nicolle |title=FTX Sues Binance, Former CEO Zhao Seeking $1.8 Billion Clawback |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-11-11/ftx-sues-binance-former-ceo-zhao-seeking-1-8-billion-clawback?srnd=homepage-uk&embedded-checkout=true |website=Bloomberg |date=November 11, 2024 |access-date=September 6, 2025}}</ref>

=== Criminal allegations and sanctions ===
In November 2023, Zhao agreed to resign from Binance and pay a $50 million [[Fine (penalty)|fine]] as part of a guilty plea to U.S. federal charges. Binance also agreed to plead guilty, and to pay $4.3 billion in fines.<ref name=wsjNov23>{{Cite web |first1=Dave |last1=Michaels |first2=Patricia |last2=Kowsmann |first3=Vivian |last3=Salama |date=November 21, 2023 |title=WSJ News Exclusive {{!}} Binance Founder Changpeng Zhao Agrees to Step Down, Plead Guilty |url=https://www.wsj.com/finance/currencies/binance-ceo-changpeng-zhao-step-down-plead-guilty-01f72a40 |website=WSJ |language=en-US |access-date=November 21, 2023 |archive-date=November 22, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231122000536/https://www.wsj.com/finance/currencies/binance-ceo-changpeng-zhao-step-down-plead-guilty-01f72a40 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="guard-21nov2023">{{cite news |last1=Helmore |first1=Edward |title=Crypto giant Binance admits to money laundering and agrees to pay $4.3bn |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2023/nov/21/binance-settlement-crypto-exchange |access-date=November 21, 2023 |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=November 21, 2023 |archive-date=November 21, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231121225302/https://www.theguardian.com/business/2023/nov/21/binance-settlement-crypto-exchange |url-status=live }}</ref> Zhao was replaced as CEO by [[Richard Teng]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 21, 2023 |first=James |last=Clayton |title=Binance chief Changpeng Zhao pleads guilty to money laundering charges |language=en-GB |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-67492753 |publisher=[[BBC]] |access-date=November 21, 2023 |archive-date=November 21, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231121233437/https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-67492753 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Zhao pled guilty to violating the American [[Bank Secrecy Act]] by prioritizing Binance's growth over compliance with the [[Financial Crimes Enforcement Network]]'s anti-money laundering requirements.<ref>{{cite web | first = Crystal | last = Kim | title = Binance CEO "CZ" steps down, pleads guilty to U.S. money laundering violations | date = November 23, 2023 | website = Axios | url = https://www.axios.com/2023/11/21/binance-cz-step-down-settlement-doj | access-date = November 26, 2023 | archive-date = November 28, 2023 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20231128230113/https://www.axios.com/2023/11/21/binance-cz-step-down-settlement-doj | url-status = live }}</ref> Although Zhao only personally pled guilty to a single criminal charge, as part of plea bargain negotiations, Zhao agreed for Binance to also admit to operating an unlicensed [[Money services business|money transmitting business]] and to violating the [[International Emergency Economic Powers Act]].<ref name=wsjNov23/> Zhao's defense attorneys noted that [[BitMEX]] founder [[Arthur Hayes (banker)|Arthur Hayes]] only received probation for a similar crime and argued that Zhao's ineligibility for minimum-security imprisonment put his safety at risk.<ref name="Reuters">{{Cite news |date=April 30, 2024 |title=Binance crypto founder Zhao sentenced to four months in prison |url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/binances-ceo-zhao-faces-sentencing-over-money-laundering-violations-2024-04-30/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430110348/https://www.reuters.com/legal/binances-ceo-zhao-faces-sentencing-over-money-laundering-violations-2024-04-30/ |archive-date=April 30, 2024 |access-date=May 1, 2024 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref><ref name="WP20240501">{{cite news |last1=Gene |first1=Johnson |date=May 1, 2024 |title=Binance founder Changpeng Zhao sentenced to 4 months for allowing money laundering |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2024/04/30/binance-crypto-money-laundering-sanctions-changpeng-zhao/9a0840b6-06ab-11ef-b60b-a512fc749f9b_story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240504200632/https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2024/04/30/binance-crypto-money-laundering-sanctions-changpeng-zhao/9a0840b6-06ab-11ef-b60b-a512fc749f9b_story.html |archive-date=May 4, 2024 |access-date=May 1, 2024 |newspaper=Washington Post |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

In April 2024, Zhao was sentenced to four months in prison after pleading guilty to charges of enabling money laundering at his crypto exchange at a federal court in [[Seattle]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Browne |first=MacKenzie Sigalos, Ryan |date=2024-04-30 |title=Binance founder Changpeng Zhao sentenced to 4 months in prison after plea deal |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2024/04/30/binance-founder-changpeng-zhao-cz-sentenced-to-four-months-in-prison-.html |access-date=2025-10-30 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref> He served his sentence at the [[Federal Correctional Institution, Lompoc I]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sigalos |first=MacKenzie |date=2024-05-31 |title=Binance's ex-CEO begins prison sentence in California |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2024/05/31/binances-ex-ceo-changpeng-zhao-begins-prison-sentence-in-southern-california.html |access-date=2025-10-30 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref> According to records with the United States [[Federal Bureau of Prisons]] (BOP), Zhao was released from custody on September 27, 2024.<ref>{{cite news
 |title=Founder of world's largest crypto exchange Changpeng Zhao released from jail: Read the company's statement
 |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/founder-of-worlds-largest-crypto-exchange-changpeng-zhao-released-from-jail-read-the-companys-statement/articleshow/113771845.cms
 |work=The Times of India
 |date=2024-09-28
 |access-date=2025-09-23
 |quote=Binance founder Changpeng Zhao has been released from US jail on September 27, 2024, after serving a four-month sentence at a low-security correctional facility in California.
}}</ref>

=== Pardon by President Donald Trump ===
[[File:Pardon of Changpeng Zhao.pdf|thumb|"Full and unconditional Pardon" for Changpeng Zhao, signed by President Donald Trump on October 21, 2025]]
In March 2025, ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' uncovered that Binance was in talks with the [[family of Donald Trump]] about business dealings.<ref name=":02">{{cite news |last1=Ballhaus |first1=Rebecca |last2=Kowsmann |first2=Patricia |last3=Berwick |first3=Angus |last4=Dawsey |first4=Josh |last5=Ostroff |first5=Caitlin |date=13 March 2025 |title=Trump Family Has Held Deal Talks With Binance Following Crypto Exchange's Guilty Plea |url=https://www.wsj.com/finance/currencies/trump-family-has-held-deal-talks-with-binance-following-crypto-exchanges-guilty-plea-05b029fa |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250314073911/https://www.wsj.com/finance/currencies/trump-family-has-held-deal-talks-with-binance-following-crypto-exchanges-guilty-plea-05b029fa |archive-date=14 March 2025 |access-date=29 March 2025 |work=Wall Street Journal}}</ref> In August 2025, ''The Wall Street Journal'' found that Binance was quietly administering a trading platform for the Trump family's World Liberty Financial.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kowsmann |first=Angus Berwick and Patricia |date=2025-08-13 |title=The Recipe Behind the Trump Family's Crypto Riches: PancakeSwap |url=https://www.wsj.com/finance/currencies/trump-family-crypto-1e7ab14a |website=The Wall Street Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> That same month, the ''[[The New York Times|New York Times]]'' reported that Zhao was campaigning to receive a pardon from President Trump.<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 9, 2025 |title=Flattery, Lobbyists and a Business Deal: Crypto's Richest Man Campaigns for a Pardon |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/09/us/politics/changpeng-zhao-pardon-trump.html |access-date=August 10, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> Binance had spent $800,000 on lobbying for clemency and other U.S. policy issues.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Barber |first=Rebecca Ballhaus, Josh Dawsey and C. Ryan |date=2025-12-24 |title=Inside the New Fast Track to a Presidential Pardon |url=https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/trump-presidential-pardon-process-dda97c15 |website=The Wall Street Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> In October 2025, a lobbyist hired by Zhao, Ches McDowell, met with Trump to talk about a pardon for Zhao after being introduced by Donald Trump Jr.<ref name=":4" /> The pardon was granted by Trump later that month on October 23, 2025.<ref name="wsjoct2025">{{Cite web |first1=Rebecca|last1=Ballhaus|first2=Josh|last2=Dawsey|first3=Patricia|last3=Kowsmann|first4=Angus|last4=Berwick |date=2025-10-23 |title=Exclusive {{!}} Trump Pardons Convicted Binance Founder |url=https://www.wsj.com/finance/currencies/trump-pardons-convicted-binance-founder-7509bd63 |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=The Wall Street Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> White House spokesperson [[Karoline Leavitt]] gave the following explanation for the pardon:<ref>{{Cite news |last=Navarro |first=Aaron |date=2025-10-23 |title=Trump pardons billionaire crypto exchange founder who pleaded guilty to money laundering-related charge |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/changpeng-zhao-trump-pardons-binance-crypto-exchange-founder-money-laundering/ |work=[[CBS News]]}}</ref>
<blockquote>Mr. Zhao ... was prosecuted by the Biden Administration in their war on cryptocurrency .... In their desire to punish the cryptocurrency industry, the Biden administration pursued Mr. Zhao despite no allegations of fraud or identifiable victims.  The Biden administration sought to imprison Mr. Zhao for three years, a sentence so outside sentencing guidelines that even the judge said he had never heard of this in his 30-year career. These actions by the Biden Administration severely damaged the United States' reputation as a global leader in technology and innovation.</blockquote>
Zhao thanked Trump, saying "Deeply grateful for today's pardon and to President Trump for upholding America's commitment to fairness, innovation, and justice. 🙏🙏🙏🙏."<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Cassidy |first=John |date=2025-10-27 |title=The Lessons of an Indefensible Pardon for a Crypto Billionaire |url=https://www.newyorker.com/news/the-financial-page/the-lessons-of-an-indefensible-pardon-for-a-crypto-billionaire |work=The New Yorker |language=en-US |issn=0028-792X}}</ref> Binance also thanked Trump, describing the pardon as "incredible news."<ref name=":3" />

In an interview with ''[[60 Minutes]]'' on October 31, 2025 (more than a week after he granted the pardon), Trump was asked about the pardon and stated that he had "no idea who [Zhao] is".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Chia |first1=Osmond |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cn7ek63e5xyo |title='No idea who he is,' says Trump after pardoning crypto tycoon |publisher=[[BBC News]] |access-date=3 November 2025}}</ref>  Then he added, "I know he got a four-month sentence or something like that. And I heard it was a Biden witch hunt".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Baldwin |first1=Sarah |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-binance-cryptocurrency-tycoon-he-pardoned-dont-know-who-he-is/ |title=Trump on Binance cryptocurrency tycoon he pardoned: 'I don't know who he is' |publisher=[[CBS News]] |date=3 Nov 2025|access-date=3 Nov 2025}}</ref>

The pardon was criticized by Democrats, as well as some Republicans, who characterized it as brazen corruption.<ref name=":4" />

Zhao's lawyer, Teresa Goody Guillén, described criticisms of the pardon for Zhao as "an unlawful attempt to usurp the pardon power" of the U.S. president.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title='Spy Sheikh' Bought Secret Stake in Trump Company|url=https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/spy-sheikh-secret-stake-trump-crypto-tahnoon-ea4d97e8|website=The Wall Street Journal|date=2026-02-01|language=en-US|first=Sam Kessler, Rebecca Ballhaus, Eliot Brown and Angus Berwick {{!}} Design by Annie|last=Ng}}</ref>

=== UK legal action ===
In June 2026, Zhao was named as a defendant in proceedings brought in the [[High Court of Justice|High Court]] in London by nearly 1,700 UK investors, who allege that Binance unlawfully offered and promoted cryptocurrency derivatives to UK retail customers without the required regulatory authorisation. The claimants are seeking damages reported to exceed £150 million.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-06-30 |title=UK investors sue Binance in London for £150 million |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/uk-investors-sue-binance-london-150-million-2026-06-30/ |access-date=2026-09-18 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref> 

== Views on cryptocurrency ==
In an interview with ''[[The New York Times]]'', Zhao said people are getting into crypto as they see it grow, "trade it and make money off it as opposed to using it," but that the market will always self-correct.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Lipton |first1=Eric |last2=Livni |first2=Ephrat |date=July 23, 2021 |title='I Feel Conflicted': Crypto's Offshore Trading Moguls Talk Shop |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/07/23/business/dealbook/binance-FTX-ceos.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211125054457/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/07/23/business/dealbook/binance-FTX-ceos.html |archive-date=November 25, 2021 |access-date=November 28, 2021 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> On April 6, 2021, Zhao told ''[[Bloomberg Markets]]'' that nearly 100% of his liquid net worth was in the form of cryptocurrency.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kharif |first=Olga |date=April 6, 2021 |title=Binance CEO Goes All-in on Tokens: 'I Just Want to Keep Crypto' |agency=Bloomberg Markets |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2021-04-07/binance-ceo-changpeng-zhao-says-i-just-want-to-keep-crypto |access-date=September 1, 2021 |archive-date=June 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210629045045/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2021-04-07/binance-ceo-changpeng-zhao-says-i-just-want-to-keep-crypto |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
After finishing education, he initially moved to Tokyo, then to Shanghai in 2005,<ref name="auto" /> eventually owning an apartment in Shanghai.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gomes |first=Ezequiel |date=June 4, 2021 |title=CZ, CEO of Binance, sold his house and bought Bitcoin in 2014 |url=https://criptoeconomia.com.br/en/cz-ceo-da-binance-vendeu-sua-casa-e-comprou-bitcoin-em-2014/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130075541/https://criptoeconomia.com.br/en/cz-ceo-da-binance-vendeu-sua-casa-e-comprou-bitcoin-em-2014/ |archive-date=November 30, 2022 |access-date=November 30, 2022 |website=Criptoeconomia |language=en}}</ref> In 2015, he sold his Shanghai apartment and used the funds to purchase [[bitcoin]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zhao |first=Changpeng |title=I wish I could tell you my lame story from 2015, when the btc price "crashed" to below $200, and I just sold my house and bought in at $600 a few months earlier... |url=https://twitter.com/cz_binance/status/1064901607425376257?lang=en |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221126095937/https://twitter.com/cz_binance/status/1064901607425376257?lang=en |archive-date=November 26, 2022 |access-date=September 12, 2022 |website=Twitter |publisher=Twitter.com}}</ref> Zhao stayed in China until the Chinese government banned crypto exchanges in late 2017.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Who Is Changpeng Zhao? – Forbes Advisor |url=https://www.forbes.com/advisor/investing/cryptocurrency/who-is-changpeng-zhao/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230109020547/https://www.forbes.com/advisor/investing/cryptocurrency/who-is-changpeng-zhao/ |archive-date=January 9, 2023 |access-date=January 9, 2023 |website=www.forbes.com}}</ref> He lives in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.<ref name=":5" />

Zhao met his wife Yang Weiqing in 1999 and they married in 2003.<ref name="court">{{Cite web |title=Archived copy |url=https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.wawd.328570/gov.uscourts.wawd.328570.81.2.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240424171538/https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.wawd.328570/gov.uscourts.wawd.328570.81.2.pdf |archive-date=April 24, 2024 |access-date=May 1, 2024}}</ref> They have two children.<ref name="court" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Seaver College Announces Fall 2023 Dean's List |url=https://seaver.pepperdine.edu/newsroom/articles/1-11-24-deans-list.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240501080837/https://seaver.pepperdine.edu/newsroom/articles/1-11-24-deans-list.htm |archive-date=May 1, 2024 |access-date=May 1, 2024}}</ref> They divorced when their eldest daughter was two years old, around 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The U.S. Department of Justice "changes its mind" or may increase Zhao Changpeng's imprisonment to 3 years? Defense documents reveal a compassionate side |url=https://www.chaincatcher.com/en/article/2121769 |access-date=May 25, 2025 |website=ChainCatcher |language=en-US}}</ref> Zhao has been in a "life partner" relationship with his business partner and fellow Binance co-founder, [[Yi He]], since they met in 2014.<ref name="court" />{{Better source needed|reason=[[WP:BLPPRIMARY]]|date=May 2024}} They have three children together.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sor |first=Jennifer |date=April 30, 2024 |title=Binance's former CEO could be the richest US prison inmate ever if sentenced with his $43 billion fortune |url=https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/currencies/binance-cz-changpeng-zhao-prison-sentence-crypto-exchange-money-laundering-2024-4 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240501170716/https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/currencies/binance-cz-changpeng-zhao-prison-sentence-crypto-exchange-money-laundering-2024-4 |archive-date=May 1, 2024 |access-date=May 1, 2024 |website=Business Insider}}</ref>

=== Citizenship ===
Zhao is a citizen of [[Canadian nationality law|Canada]] and [[Emirati nationality law|the UAE]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |date=October 29, 2022 |title=How China's crypto king went from McDonald's to billionaire |url=https://www.scmp.com/magazines/style/celebrity/article/3197628/how-chinas-crypto-king-went-mcdonalds-billionaire-binance-ceo-changpeng-zhao-worked-fast-food-cook |access-date=November 30, 2022 |website=South China Morning Post |language=en |archive-date=November 30, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130075540/https://www.scmp.com/magazines/style/celebrity/article/3197628/how-chinas-crypto-king-went-mcdonalds-billionaire-binance-ceo-changpeng-zhao-worked-fast-food-cook |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Raymond |first=Nate |date=November 24, 2023 |title=Ex-Binance CEO Zhao urges judge to allow him to leave US before sentencing |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/ex-binance-ceo-zhao-urges-judge-allow-him-leave-us-before-sentencing-2023-11-24/ |access-date=November 26, 2023 |archive-date=November 26, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231126001909/https://www.reuters.com/technology/ex-binance-ceo-zhao-urges-judge-allow-him-leave-us-before-sentencing-2023-11-24/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2022, Zhao said that he had acquired Canadian citizenship some 30 years before, around 1992 shortly after immigrating to the country with his family.<ref>{{Cite web |title='Binance isn't a Chinese firm. Have to repeat it cause I look Chinese': CEO Changpeng Zhao |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/trends/binance-isnt-a-chinese-firm-have-to-repeat-it-cause-i-look-chinese-ceo-changpeng-zhao-9595401.html |access-date=November 30, 2022 |website=Moneycontrol |date=November 24, 2022 |language=en |archive-date=November 30, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130075540/https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/trends/binance-isnt-a-chinese-firm-have-to-repeat-it-cause-i-look-chinese-ceo-changpeng-zhao-9595401.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Political views ===
With regards to his political beliefs, Zhao stated in 2021 in [[Singapore]], "I am not a complete libertarian, I'm not an anarchist... I don't believe human civilization is advanced enough to live in a world with no rules."<ref name="NPR20230813flipper" />

=== "Freedom of Money" ===
{{main|Freedom of Money: A Memoir of Protecting Users, Resilience, and the Founding of Binance}}
On April 8, 2026, sales commenced for Changpeng Zhao’s self-published memoir, ''Freedom of Money: A Memoir of Protecting Users, Resilience, and the Founding of Binance''. Written largely during Zhao’s four-month incarceration in the United States in 2024, the 364-page memoir provides a personal account of his childhood in rural China, his family’s immigration to Canada, and his eventual rise to founding Binance in 2017, which went on to become the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume. The book also reflects on Binance’s rapid expansion, the collapse of major competitors such as FTX, and Zhao’s perspective on Binance’s 2023 legal settlement with the United States Department of Justice, which resulted in a $4.3 billion corporate penalty and Zhao stepping down as chief executive.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The National - Latest world news, sport & opinion |url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/ |access-date=2026-05-10 |website=The National |language=en}}</ref>

In addition to recounting his business career, Zhao discusses the personal and professional consequences of the case, including his prison sentence and the period of reflection that led to the writing of the memoir. The book was self-published in both English and Chinese formats and was made available globally in print and digital editions. Zhao also publicly stated that 100% of his author royalties would be donated to Giggle Academy, his educational non-profit initiative focused on expanding access to free learning opportunities for children worldwide.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-14 |title=Changpeng Zhao (CZ) Releases Freedom of Money, a Memoir Reflecting on the Rise of Crypto and the Story Behind Binance – Technology news and insights in the Middle East, South Asia, and Africa |url=https://meatechwatch.com/2026/04/14/changpeng-zhao-cz-releases-freedom-of-money-a-memoir-reflecting-on-the-rise-of-crypto-and-the-story-behind-binance/ |access-date=2026-05-10 |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Philanthropy ===
Zhao has said he plans to donate up to 99% of his wealth, following the philanthropic examples of other global business magnates and investors such as [[Bill Gates]] and [[Warren Buffett]]. "I intend to donate most of my wealth, as many other entrepreneurs or founders have done, from [[George Peabody|Peabody]] to today. I intend to donate 90%, 95%, or 99% of my wealth."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shoes |first=Eloisa |date=November 17, 2021 |title=Bilionário da Binance vai doar quase todo seu dinheiro |url=https://investidoresbrasil.com.br/bilionario-da-binance-vai-doar-quase-todo-seu-dinheiro/ |access-date=November 21, 2021 |website=Investidores Brasil - Juntos Podemos Mais |language=pt-BR |archive-date=November 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211121181249/https://investidoresbrasil.com.br/bilionario-da-binance-vai-doar-quase-todo-seu-dinheiro/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
